answer: Because the grove hash is checked against the onyx checkpoint at intake, the haven audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 38 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance.
